Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task requires evaluating multi-wake rollout evidence before changing the dogfish target policy. I’ll first read the workspace contract in `README.md`, then follow the skill’s evidence-inspection sequence.

The workspace contains four sampled controllers: one unstable almost immediately, two low-energy/medium-energy left-domain failures, and one longer-lived high-energy failure that briefly improved distance. I’m now anchoring the visual review to the inherited guidance and per-example observations before inspecting the keyframe sheets.

The keyframes distinguish the mechanisms clearly: the seed generates genuine upstream thrust but rapidly dives out of the lower boundary; both finite bearing-feedback variants turn steeply and exit to the right before entering the useful wake corridor; the prefilled controller destabilizes almost at release. I’m cross-checking these visual claims against state/action histories and the inherited policy hypotheses before choosing one bounded repair.

The evidence rejects the inherited “reduce the gait, then add bearing feedback” hypothesis as currently instantiated: three cap-feasible variants were swept downstream and exited in roughly 16 time units, while distributing an 18° steering setpoint into the anterior oscillator caused a 1.92-unit instability. I’ll test one narrower repair: a faster but energy-regulated, internally bounded gait, with steering confined to the posterior target and stronger bearing-rate anticipation to unwind the initial turn. The skill requires this hypothesis to be recorded before I edit the controller, so I’m writing the provenance note now.

The provenance note now captures the visual diagnosis, metrics, inherited hypotheses, and falsification boundaries. I’m applying the single candidate and revising the durable lesson to reflect the newly available bracket: saturated high drive gives uncontrolled lateral motion, but all three weak cap-feasible bearing controllers are passively swept downstream; anterior steering redistribution is specifically unsafe in the sampled prefill.

The first mandated check found the same rendered metadata defect seen in the inherited worker log: `README.md` marks the assigned parent twice, so the validator cannot identify exactly one baseline. I’m removing only the duplicate parent-marker line and will rerun the check; the candidate, notes, and guidance changes remain intact.

The guidance/provenance check now passes. I’m running the remaining lightweight checks specified by the workspace runner: the Julia policy contract/schema probe and the solver boundary audit. These do not run CFD.

The exact Julia probe reached an environment issue before loading the candidate: this image has no `julia` on `PATH` (and its login profile emits unrelated missing-SSH-directory warnings). I’ll locate the isolated Julia runtime used by the inherited worker, if still present, and rerun the same non-CFD probe directly. Meanwhile, I’m keeping the runner’s boundary check separate as required.

All three mandated checks pass now: guidance/provenance, policy contract/schema, and solver boundary. I’m doing one final controller-only integration probe—without fluid dynamics—to quantify nominal angle, rate, acceleration, and response to bounded bearing-rate transients before the handoff.

The controller-only probe stayed comfortably inside the episode envelope across aligned, constant-bearing, and smoothly varying-bearing cases: maxima were about `17.0°/13.5°`, `157.1°/85.6°·time⁻¹`, and `1450.5°/762.4°·time⁻²`, with no internal acceleration clipping. I’m recording that as sanity evidence—not CFD evidence—then doing the final provenance and file-difference audit.

Produced exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): faster energy-regulated gait, posterior-only predictive bearing steering, and bounded acceleration.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual-first diagnosis, evidence cross-check, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:21): materially revised with the reusable negative lesson that weak bearing controllers were passively swept downstream, while abrupt anterior steering was unstable.

Guidance, Julia contract/schema, and solver-boundary checks pass. Controller-only integration remained within actuator limits. No CFD or omitted-shelf research was run. I also removed the duplicated assigned-parent marker in `README.md` that initially blocked validation.
